title: QuEra Computing and Lawrence Berkeley National Lab Observe Prethermal Dynamical Phase Transitions on 180 Qubits in Nature Study - Quantum Computing Report
gist: NERSC (Berkeley Lab), QuEra, Harvard and Boston University published in Nature quench-dynamics experiments on up to 180 neutral-atom qubits on QuEra's Aquila via Amazon Braket, observing prethermal steady states, resonant melting and a first-order 2D dynamical phase transition, benchmarked with Bloqade on Perlmutter. QuEra and AWS also released a survey of 55 papers run on Aquila since 2022, ahead of QuEra's planned 2028 fault-tolerant Libra system.

insights.claim: Researchers from NERSC at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, QuEra Computing, Harvard and Boston University published in Nature non-equilibrium quantum quench dynamics on up to 180 neutral-atom qubits using QuEra's analog Aquila processor via Amazon Braket.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A Nature publication from the cloud-accessible Aquila validates QuEra's analog platform for frontier physics and supports its credibility ahead of fault-tolerant products.
insights.locator: Researchers from the National Energy Research Scientific Computing Center

insights.claim: Experiments on 1D chains of up to 52 rubidium-87 atoms and 2D square lattices up to 180 atoms, quenched from an all-ground state at a Rabi frequency of 2.5 MHz, uncovered long-lived Floquet-like prethermal steady states, structured resonant melting at multi-excitation island resonances, and a first-order dynamical phase transition in 2D driven by Neel-order defect proliferation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows analog neutral-atom machines probing regimes that classical simulation cannot directly reach at this scale.
insights.locator: Following sudden parameter quenches from an all-ground initial state

insights.claim: Using a generalized Clausius-Clapeyron relation, the authors verified that the 2D dynamical transition sharpens with system size and has no counterpart in the system's equilibrium phase diagram.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A genuinely non-equilibrium phenomenon discovered at scale strengthens the scientific-discovery case for quantum simulators.
insights.quote: lacks any counterpart in the system’s equilibrium phase diagram

insights.claim: NERSC researchers benchmarked the hardware runs with exact-diagonalization simulations using QuEra's open-source Bloqade.jl on the Perlmutter supercomputer (up to 20 atoms, 100 microsecond evolution) before scaling experiments to 180 qubits on Aquila.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The HPC-validates-small, QPU-runs-large workflow is the template for national-lab quantum integration and a channel for QuEra software adoption.
insights.locator: To construct and benchmark the hardware runs

insights.claim: Classical simulation on Perlmutter validated prethermal blockade-subspace averages, site-disorder broadening (~0.1 micrometre) and finite-size scaling against the Aquila hardware runs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cross-validation with HPC is how claims from analog quantum hardware earn trust.

themes.theme: Aquila platform track record and roadmap

insights.claim: QuEra and Amazon Web Services released a four-year survey of 55 research and application papers executed on Aquila since its November 2022 launch on Amazon Braket: 24 many-body physics, 16 optimization, 8 QML/applications and 7 benchmarking/tooling/characterization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: 55 papers is a measurable usage/traction metric for a cloud-accessed quantum product, useful for gauging QuEra's ecosystem versus peers.

insights.claim: Demonstrations on Aquila span 3 to 256 atoms, including a 231-qubit maximum independent set reduction and 108-atom reservoir learning.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Optimization and ML applications on analog hardware are a nearer-term commercial angle than fault-tolerant algorithms.

insights.claim: QuEra plans a fault-tolerant system called Libra in 2028.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A dated fault-tolerance milestone to track for QuEra and the neutral-atom modality.
insights.quote: QuEra’s planned fault-tolerant Libra system in 2028
insights.locator: To construct and benchmark the hardware runs
